title: priority and type are unenforced freeform strings, not enums -- the fleet has no shared vocabulary because quest never defined one
description:
Raised by opum-agent (OPAG-177, 2026-09-17) after five repositories independently found priority/type casing and vocabulary drift while running fleet-wide dedupe passes: opum-agent (priority capitalized+lowercase mixed), quest-web (all lowercase, internally consistent: critical/high/low/medium priority, bug/chore/docs/feature/task type), opum-fleet (priority clean, but type collides with opum-sdlcs branch-prefix enum feat/fix/chore/docs/refactor/test), lore-web (mixed case, ~20/90 blank), opum-marketplace (5 feat vs 4 feature, 7 with no priority). Explicitly asked to me as the schema owner: whether this is one enum or two, and whether critical/docs are real values.

CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE, not inferred: src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts:276-277 defines both fields as `priority: z.string().optional()` and `type: z.string().optional()` -- completely unconstrained. There is no enum, no canonical set, and no validation anywhere in this repository. Every value observed across the fleet is equally valid input today. This repositorys own tracker independently confirms the same failure mode: priority has 122 high / 78 medium / 33 low / 1 stray "Low" (found and fixed in the 2026-09-17 dedupe pass); type has feature(53)/docs(49)/bug(49)/chore(38)/spike(20)/task(11)/enhancement(6) -- a SEVENTH vocabulary, sharing docs/bug/chore/feature with quest-webs set but adding spike/enhancement/task and never using critical.

MY JUDGMENT, since this is quests own schema and no one else can rule on it:
1. priority should be a real enum: low, medium, high, critical -- adopting quest-webs set, since it is the only one observed that is both internally consistent and already in real use elsewhere in the fleet, and critical is a genuine, useful distinction above high that several repos would want.
2. type should NOT be unified with opum-sdlcs branch-prefix enum. Those are two different axes that happen to share vocabulary by coincidence: type answers "what kind of work is this" (bug/feature/chore/docs/enhancement/spike), branch prefix answers "what kind of change delivers it" (feat/fix/chore/docs/refactor/test) -- a bug-type task can ship via a fix branch, an enhancement-type task can ship via a feat branch. Forcing one enum to serve both is what produced opum-fleets collision. Recommend: feature, bug, chore, docs, enhancement, spike as quests own canonical type set. "task" as a type value is meaningless (every record already is a task) and should be treated as equivalent to unset rather than a real category.
3. Enforce prospectively only, matching the convention four repositories independently reached without coordinating: validate on write, case-fold or reject unknown values for new/edited records; do not bulk-rewrite closed/historical records to match. History is reported, not rewritten -- consistent with this repositorys own retirement-scope convention for other historical records.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A canonical DEFAULT set for priority (low/medium/high/critical), workspace-configurable and written by quest init into a fresh workspace, per opum-doc ADR make-quests-type-and-priority-vocabulary-workspace-configured-with-a-canonical-default (opum-doc main 34b4b2d, amended by ODOC-318). The ADR's 'same mechanism as status' premise was corrected by ODOC-318: status is not workspace-configured at runtime, so this is the FIRST configured vocabulary, not a second instance of an existing mechanism.

A canonical DEFAULT set for type as a work-kind taxonomy (feature/bug/chore/docs/enhancement/spike, per the same ADR at opum-doc main 34b4b2d, amended by ODOC-318), workspace-configurable and written by quest init, and explicitly decoupled from opum-sdlc's branch-prefix enum. The default omits the existing quest-cli-only value task. It is neither kept in this workspace's configuration nor folded: the 11 records carrying it are left as reported history, with a stated reason (the value names no work-kind distinction -- every record is already a task -- and rewriting Done records to remove it would falsify them, the fleet's own retirement-scope convention).
Write-time validation is added (task create/edit) that rejects or case-normalizes an out-of-vocabulary value on new writes, without touching existing closed/historical records

quest manifest --json documents the workspace's configured values for both fields, so a consumer can validate client-side before writing (per opum-doc ADR make-quests-type-and-priority-vocabulary-workspace-configured-with-a-canonical-default, main 34b4b2d, amended by ODOC-318).
OPAG-177s fleet-wide check is unblocked: its first criterion was recorded as underspecified pending this decision

quest doctor reports each existing record whose type or priority is outside the workspace's configured set, naming the id, the field and the value, and never rewrites the record. Per opum-doc ADR make-quests-type-and-priority-vocabulary-workspace-configured-with-a-canonical-default (main 34b4b2d, amended by ODOC-318): historical records are reported, not rewritten.

plan: 1. Workspace config: an optional [tasks] table in .quest/workspace.toml with types = [...] and priorities = [...]. It is parsed and validated in readConfiguration (non-empty, unique case-insensitively, strings). Absent means unconfigured (option A, pending the orchestrator), so writes are open and doctor stays silent

2. Domain: a TaskVocabulary type plus a pure resolveVocabularyValue(field, value, set). An exact match is kept, a case-insensitive match is normalised to the configured spelling, anything else is refused with exit 6 naming the allowed values

3. Writes: task create, task edit and task edit-batch validate a PRESENT --type/--priority value only. Absent stays legal and clearing stays legal. Other edits to a record carrying a legacy value are untouched. Backlog migration import is never validated (opum-cli-e2e suite 41)
4. quest init writes the canonical default [tasks] table into a fresh workspace (and adds it when re-run on an existing one without one). quest-cli adopts it in its own workspace.toml
5. quest manifest --json carries the workspace configured values (or null when unconfigured or outside a workspace) under data, never as a new top-level key
6. quest doctor reports task_vocabulary_off_set per record (id, field, value, hint) across every location, and never rewrites
7. Tests for each AC with a pre-change failure, guide and help text, CHANGELOG, a reviewer pass, and bun run check
implementationNotes:
RATIFIED by quest-web, 2026-09-17, the repo whose vocabulary this proposal adopts (asked directly per this tasks own AC1, not assumed). Self-measured their full 53-task tracker (both with and without --include-archived): priority is exactly {critical, high, medium, low}, type is exactly {bug, chore, docs, feature, task}, zero case or spelling drift across every set value -- so the consistency this proposal banks on is real, not a small-sample artifact.

CRITICAL AMENDMENT to AC3, from quest-web: the enum must be `z.enum([...]).optional()`, NOT required-non-null. 9 of quest-webs 53 records have priority entirely unset (null, not an invalid value) -- all Done/historical. A required-non-null enum would force a breaking backfill migration on their existing data. Verified the same pattern holds here: 92 of this repositorys own task records also have priority unset. Any implementation of this task MUST keep the field optional; only a PRESENT value is validated against the enum, absence stays legal.

New dispatch from opum-agent, 2026-09-18 12:44Z, user-approved, relayed via this session: item 2 of a 4-item batch asked for task `type` specifically, described as still an unenforced free string across the fleet (independent of this task, no reference to QCLI-330 by id). Filing it here instead of as a duplicate task -- same underlying defect (type is z.string().optional() with no vocabulary), but the requested SHAPE differs from this task's AC2/judgment section, which proposes one fixed, cross-fleet type enum (feature/bug/chore/docs/enhancement/spike) already argued from real fleet data.

The new ask: model `type` on the EXISTING quest status pattern instead -- `task status-flow` reports a workspace-configured status set (statuses/terminalStatuses/pausedStatus, per quest help task status-flow), and `quest doctor` already reports records that drift outside it (see the paused-status doctor check). Extend that same shape to `type`: a per-workspace configurable vocabulary, validated on write, drift reported by doctor -- explicitly NOT one hardcoded fleet-wide enum, on the stated reasoning that a vocabulary right for this fleet would be wrong for an unrelated quest workspace.

This is a real tension with AC2 as currently written, not just an alternative phrasing: AC2 asks to ratify one shared type enum; the new ask asks for per-workspace configurability with no single ratified set. It does NOT touch `priority` (AC1), which the new dispatch did not mention and which already has the quest-web ratification recorded in this task's implementation notes.

Not resolving this here -- flagging it so whoever picks up this task chooses between (a) one fixed enum for type as already scoped, (b) configurable-per-workspace type matching status-flow, or (c) both: a quest-cli-shipped default type vocabulary that a workspace can override, closest to how status-flow itself likely already works. Worth checking how status-flow's own configurability is implemented (workspace.toml or similar) before choosing, since it is the precedent this ask explicitly cites.

2026-09-28: the design is RULED. QCLI-330 no longer waits on OPAG-216. The ruling is opum-doc ADR make-quests-type-and-priority-vocabulary-workspace-configured-with-a-canonical-default, read by ref at opum-doc main ae4574c, not taken from the relay. It is a HYBRID. Type and priority become workspace-configured on the same mechanism as status (LifecyclePolicy). Quest ships the canonical set as the default that quest init writes. Write-time validation rejects or case-normalizes against the workspace's set. Historical records are reported, not rewritten.

At the orchestrator's request, AC1 and AC2 were amended from "a canonical enum" to "a canonical DEFAULT set, workspace-configurable", and AC4 from "the enum values" to "the workspace's configured values". AC3 and AC5 are unchanged. Nothing had been ticked, so no state was lost.

Implementation stays in the queue after QCLI-331.
2026-09-28: added AC6, the reporting half of the ADR's 'historical records are reported, not rewritten'. AC3 covered only the not-rewriting. The orchestrator approved it by cross-session message.

2026-09-28 RULING, orchestrator opum-agent (session 6bf3cbb3): option A. A workspace with no configured type/priority set is OPEN, meaning no write validation and no doctor report. quest init writes the canonical default into a fresh workspace, and quest-cli's own workspace.toml adopts it in the same PR.

Basis, measured here and confirmed by the orchestrator at origin/dev: createTaskService (src/cli/composition.ts:136) always passes defaultTaskLifecyclePolicy, and readConfiguration (local-workspaces.ts:178-209) reads only name, taskIdPrefix and [agents]. So status is not workspace-configured at runtime, the ADR's ground (c) is false as written, and QCLI-330 is the FIRST configured vocabulary. opum-doc is recording an ADR amendment; cite its record id here once it is reported. The fleet recovers ground (d) through opum-agent OPAG-679 (each fleet tracker adopts the default by its own PR) and OPAG-177 AC8 (an unconfigured fleet workspace fails Tracker integrity).

Two constraints on the build:
(1) quest manifest --json must distinguish open from configured with an explicit marker, never an empty list.
(2) Re-running init on an existing workspace only ADDS the default when no set is configured, and never overwrites a configured one. Both directions must be proven by tests.

Consumer sweep, by ref on origin/dev: lore-cli src/adapters/quest.ts:471-497 never writes type or priority. opum-cli-e2e suite 45 writes bug/high (in set). Suite 41 needs Backlog import to preserve "Medium"/"High" verbatim, so migration is never validated.

RESTART HANDOFF, 2026-09-28 ~18:35Z. The operator is rebooting the machine; relayed by opum-agent. QCLI-330 is BUILT, NOT LANDED. Branch feat/QCLI-330-task-vocabulary: code commit c18415e2, and this note is the commit after it. It is pushed, and there is NO PR yet.

DONE, on the branch:
- [tasks] types/priorities in .quest/workspace.toml, parsed by tomlTaskVocabulary in local-workspaces.ts. A malformed table fails closed (exit 6).
- quest init writes the canonical default.
- A bare `init --reconfigure` is now accepted. It adds the default only when neither field is configured and never changes a configured set.
- TaskService validates in create, editOn and editBatch (per item), through resolveVocabularyPatch in src/domain/tasks/vocabulary.ts. Only a value the write carries is checked, and a case-only difference is normalized. Anything else exits 6 with input {field,value,allowed}.
- The manifest carries data.taskVocabulary {types, priorities}, where null means open.
- Doctor reports task_vocabulary_off_set in every location and rewrites nothing.
- quest-cli adopted the default through `init --reconfigure`. Doctor now reports 15 issues (11 type=task, 4 case-only priorities), matching the measured population.
- Guide, help and CHANGELOG updated.

EVIDENCE: bun run check exits 0 (951 pass, 0 fail), and lore check exits 0. test/qcli330-task-vocabulary.test.ts has 16 tests. 12 of them go red against pre-change origin/dev source; the 4 that pass pin open-workspace behaviour that must hold. Mutation: removing case-normalization turned exactly the predicted 2 cases red (create normalize, edit-batch).

NOT DONE:
(a) The opum-workflow:reviewer pass was in flight at the reboot and died with the machine. Re-run it on the branch.
(b) Push, open the PR, and let it go green.
(c) Tick the ACs with that evidence. AC5: OPAG-177 at opum-agent 9a29f69 reads the vocabulary from configuration (its AC7 and AC8), and this provides it. Its CI check can run only once a quest release ships this.
(d) Cite the opum-doc ADR amendment's record id once opum-doc reports it.
(e) Close the task in that same PR. Then promote dev to main with the next landing; dev d290a87 is one tracker-only commit ahead of main 30148e9.

RULING (orchestrator opum-agent 6bf3cbb3, option A). BUILD CONSTRAINTS, both met and tested:
(1) The manifest distinguishes open (null) from configured, never with an empty list.
(2) Re-running init only ADDS the default when no set is configured and never overwrites one. Tested in both directions, including a one-field set.

LESSON: in zsh an unquoted $A holding flags is ONE argument. Inline the actor flags.

REVIEWER VERDICT: BLOCK. The opum-workflow:reviewer finished before the reboot. It reviewed c18415e2; the source is identical at c002fc2. Nothing has been fixed yet, so fix these on this branch (add commits, no rebase) before opening the PR.

1. HIGH, confirmed. local-workspaces.ts:61 decides whether [tasks] exists with a line regex, not the parsed TOML. These valid spellings all read as OPEN: `[tasks] # c`, `[ tasks ]`, `["tasks"]`, the inline `tasks = {...}`, and dotted `tasks.priorities = [...]`. So does a table whose keys are misspelled (type or priority singular). A bare `init --reconfigure` then OVERWRITES that configured set with the default, which breaks ruling constraint 2. Fix: decide from the parse result ("tasks" in parsed). A present table with no known keys, or with unknown keys, is invalid_configuration.

2. HIGH, confirmed. main.ts:1335-1353 rethrows EVERY invalid_configuration, including a bad agents.skill_source, and taskService() also backs reads. The result: a workspace with no [tasks] table but a bogus skill_source gets exit 6 on task list, manifest, doctor and create, where dev gives exit 0. That breaks ruling A and the CHANGELOG claim. A malformed [tasks] also breaks every read, including manifest (which breaks lore's adapter probe) and doctor. Fix: give [tasks] errors their own code and rethrow only that. Resolve the vocabulary on write paths only. Decide whether reads survive a bad table; one option is for doctor to report it.

3. MEDIUM, confirmed. A bare `init --reconfigure` on an already-configured workspace rewrites the whole file, dropping comments and unknown tables. The help text (command-help.ts:47) says it "changes nothing but the [tasks] vocabulary", which is false. Fix: write nothing when there is nothing to add.

4. LOW. When the file also has [tasks], any unrelated TOML error is misattributed to the [tasks] table and blocks reads.
5. LOW. QUEST_TASK_STORE switches validation off. The comment at main.ts:1330 is inaccurate.
6. LOW, plausible. toLocaleLowerCase depends on locale; pin en-US or use toLowerCase.
7. NIT. Batch per-item errors lack the {field,value,allowed} fields.
8. NIT. An unreadable workspace.toml (EACCES) silently reads as open.

TEST GAPS: alternate TOML spellings and misspelled keys; read-path behaviour on a bad config (including the skill_source case); a syntactically invalid file; a bare reconfigure that should write nothing. The migration-verbatim test is a unit test on the wrong object: promote the reviewer's end-to-end run to a CLI test (init, backlog migrate High/Medium/Story, values preserved, doctor reports them).

AC TEXT, before ticking: AC1 cites "the same LifecyclePolicy mechanism as status", which is false by design, so amend it (object form plus --if-revision). AC2 needs a stated REASON for leaving the 11 type=task records as reported history, not just the consequence.

Reviewer-verified sound: every type/priority write path goes through create/editOn/editBatch. Migration is never validated (end to end: High/Medium/Story kept verbatim). Envelope order is unchanged. Doctor covers completed/. The consumers (lore data.commands, e2e suites 41/45) are safe.

2026-09-28, post-reboot: all reviewer BLOCK findings are fixed on this branch (add commits only, no rebase).
- HIGH 1: [tasks] presence is now decided from the PARSED TOML ("tasks" in parsed), not a line regex. `[ tasks ]`, `["tasks"]`, inline `tasks = {...}` and dotted `tasks.priorities = [...]` all read as configured. A table declaring neither types nor priorities (including a misspelled key) throws invalid_task_vocabulary, so it can never read as open and be overwritten. Unknown keys beside a recognised one are ignored, like [agents].
- HIGH 2: invalid_task_vocabulary is a new WorkspaceError code, distinct from invalid_configuration. The CLI carries it in a TaskVocabularyContext instead of throwing: writes (create/editOn/editBatch) refuse with it, the manifest reports both fields null, doctor reports task_vocabulary_invalid, and every read carries on. A bad agents.skill_source no longer fails task list/manifest/create, and agents --check still refuses it.
- MEDIUM: reconfigureWorkspace compares the merged config to the current one and writes NOTHING when nothing changes, so comments and unknown tables survive a no-op run.
- LOWs: a parse failure is attributed to [tasks] only when a [tasks]-looking section exists; the QUEST_TASK_STORE comment now states the override reads no workspace configuration; vocabularyKey keeps toLocaleLowerCase to stay consistent with the task-list fold (documented).
- Evidence: bun run check exits 0 (957 pass, 0 fail). test/qcli330-task-vocabulary.test.ts has 22 tests; 18 go red against pre-change origin/dev source. lore check exits 0.
- The ADR amendment is ODOC-318, read at opum-doc main 34b4b2d. AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC6 texts were amended to cite it, AC2 now carries the stated reason for leaving the 11 type=task records as reported history.
NEXT: fresh opum-workflow:reviewer pass, then the PR, tick the ACs with that evidence, and close in the same PR.

2026-09-28, second reviewer pass: SHIP-WITH-NITS. All five claimed fixes verified fixed by direct execution; rulings A/(1)/(2) hold; no new HIGH or MEDIUM. The two LOW corners it found are now ALSO fixed on this branch:
- LOW 1: the parse-failure fallback regex now recognises inline and dotted tasks spellings too, so a doubly-broken file (vocabulary config + unrelated syntax error) fails closed instead of reading as open and being overwritten. Test added: syntactically invalid workspace.toml, with and without a tasks declaration.
- LOW 2: readConfiguration computes the vocabulary BEFORE the skill_source check, so a bad agents.skill_source can no longer mask a broken [tasks] table into reading as open. Test added.
- LOW 3: CHANGELOG prose narrowed -- only create/edit/edit-batch refuse on a broken table; the other writes carry no vocabulary value and carry on, now stated deliberately.
- NIT 1: the stale QCLI-277 "checked first" comment now names the vocabulary guard as the one exception.
RECORDED FOR THE SUCCESSOR, judged out of scope here:
- NIT 2: edit-batch per-item errors carry only a message string, not the {field,value,allowed} structure the single-edit error envelope has. The message text names all three, and a machine caller can read the set from the manifest. Leave as is unless a consumer asks.
- NIT 3: an UNREADABLE workspace.toml (e.g. EACCES) silently reads as open, by design -- the broad catch at main.ts's configuredTaskVocabulary never lets a read fail. Unnamed in prose deliberately; changing it would break reads, which is the exact failure class this task fixed.
- AC6's "or quest agents --check" parenthetical was removed: agents --check does not report vocabulary drift; quest doctor is the delivered surface.
Evidence: bun run check 959 pass / 0 fail. test/qcli330-task-vocabulary.test.ts 24 tests, 20 red against pre-change origin/dev. lore check 0. agents --check --require-installed --target claude exits 0.
finalSummary: quest type and priority are now workspace-configured vocabularies instead of free strings. A [tasks] table in .quest/workspace.toml declares types/priorities; quest init writes the canonical default (feature/bug/chore/docs/enhancement/spike and low/medium/high/critical), read from the parsed TOML so every valid spelling counts. task create/edit/edit-batch validate only a value the write carries, normalizing a case-only difference to the configured spelling and exiting 6 with input.{field,value,allowed} on anything else; in a batch only the offending item fails. The manifest reports the set as data.taskVocabulary with null for an open field, never an empty list, and never fails on configuration. Doctor reports task_vocabulary_off_set per stored value in every location and task_vocabulary_invalid for a broken table, and rewrites nothing. An unconfigured workspace stays open (ODOC-318 ruling); a broken table fails closed on writes and never breaks a read; a no-op reconfigure writes nothing. Backlog migration is never validated, so imported values survive verbatim. Verified by bun run check 959/0, a 24-test suite with 20 red against pre-change source, two reviewer passes (BLOCK, then SHIP-WITH-NITS with all corners closed), and quest-cli's own doctor reporting its 15 historical records as written. PR opum-ai/quest-cli#391, CI runs 36473446897 and 36473446920.
